display_label: Dairying established across Europe
expected_effect: no directional prediction
measured_effect: Beta-lactoglobulin in calculus; 19 of 74 Eurasian individuals positive. No change point - milk is continuous across the record.

display_label: Teeth are altered for appearance, not health
expected_effect: intervention layer: first appearance; the record begins to be edited
measured_effect: 21 catalogued appliances. No denominator exists - this is a museum corpus, not a rate. Affects 21 known people over ~500 years.

display_label: Rotary querns replace saddle querns
expected_effect: wear: baseline high
measured_effect: No measured effect yet - citation still outstanding.

display_label: Sorghum and millet in the Roman diet
expected_effect: baseline
measured_effect: Sorghum and millet proteins recovered from calculus.

display_label: Roman lead production peaks
expected_effect: metals layer: sharp peak
measured_effect: Childhood enamel Pb: Iron Age Britain 0.06 mg/kg -> Roman Britain 1.21 -> Rome 3.61 -> five Empire sites 2.00-7.00 ppm. Twenty- to hundred-fold over baseline.

display_label: Water-powered milling spreads across the empire
expected_effect: wear: remains high
measured_effect: No measured effect yet - citation still outstanding.

display_label: Extraction becomes a commercial trade
expected_effect: caries: undercounted wherever extraction is available
measured_effect: 86 extracted teeth in a single deposit - the largest European intervention assemblage in this project. No population denominator: it is a drain, not a cemetery.

display_label: Coastal communities keep a low-carbohydrate diet
expected_effect: caries: coastal stays low throughout
measured_effect: Caries 0.045 coastal vs 0.171 rolling hills (3.8x). The gap WIDENS: Early modern coastal 0.030 against 0.165 overall.

display_label: Lead exposure collapses after Rome
expected_effect: metals layer: sharp fall
measured_effect: Pb falls to 0.39 mg/kg at the 360-675 exposure window, roughly two-thirds down from the Roman peak. The only signal in the dataset that falls because an economy stopped.

display_label: The first plague pandemic
expected_effect: pathogen layer: composition shifts to plague
measured_effect: Y. pestis is 86% of the 5th-century bin (19 of 22) and 60% of the 7th (12 of 20). Composition, not count - genome counts track sequencing campaigns.

display_label: Black pepper reaches central Italy
expected_effect: no direct tooth effect; trade-route evidence
measured_effect: Black pepper identified in calculus - long-distance trade recorded in the mouth.

display_label: Leprosy rises and then recedes
expected_effect: pathogen layer: composition peaks then declines

display_label: Domesday Book records thousands of watermills in England
expected_effect: wear: remains high through the medieval centuries
measured_effect: Documentary; no direct dental measurement.

display_label: Mercury used to treat leprosy and syphilis
expected_effect: metals layer: Hg elevation in specific populations
measured_effect: Mercury administered as medicine - the first case in this dataset of a metal entering the body by deliberate human act rather than by environment.

display_label: Sugar and refined starch reshape the mouth
expected_effect: caries: sustained rise to the series peak

display_label: Windmills appear in northwest Europe
expected_effect: wear: remains high
measured_effect: No measured effect yet - citation still outstanding.

display_label: Medieval lead exposure exceeds the Roman peak
expected_effect: metals layer: second and higher peak; class gradient
measured_effect: Pb 4.69 mg/kg at the 1160-1475 exposure window, above the Roman Britain figure of 1.21.

display_label: Cities become worse for teeth than the countryside
expected_effect: caries: urban exceeds rural from here
measured_effect: Urban caries exceeds rural from 1300 onward.

display_label: The Black Death
expected_effect: pathogen layer: sharp spike; tooth layer: no prediction
measured_effect: Y. pestis is 69% of all genomes in the 1300s bin (35 of 51). Hypoplasia spikes to 80.3% from 33.6% at 1200. Caries then climbs 0.101 -> 0.124 -> 0.140 across 1300-1500 as survivors diets shift. CAUTION: n=88 at 1300; osteological paradox - high LEH may mean survived stress, not only suffered it.

display_label: Syphilis epidemic spreads through Europe
expected_effect: lesion layer: rise
measured_effect: T. pallidum appears in the 1500s and 1600s bins.

display_label: New World crops reach European fields
expected_effect: caries: rise
measured_effect: New World taxa enter the food layer.

display_label: Maize and potato appear in European mouths
expected_effect: confirms crop arrival; supports the caries rise
measured_effect: Maize and potato recovered from calculus.

display_label: Tea and sugar become everyday goods in Britain
expected_effect: caries: rise begins
measured_effect: No measured effect yet - citation still outstanding.

display_label: Imported staples reach industrial workers
expected_effect: caries: peak period
measured_effect: Imported staples in the calculus of industrial workers.

display_label: Textile fibres enter workers' mouths
expected_effect: particulate layer: fibre presence
measured_effect: Cotton and wool fibres in calculus at Cross Street Chapel, Manchester - the job recorded in the mouth. NO clear microcharcoal, which the authors caution is not evidence of absent smoke exposure.

display_label: Industrial urbanisation
expected_effect: caries: peak; wear: minimum; hypoplasia: peak
measured_effect: Wear 4.35 (1200) -> 2.88 (1700); hypoplasia 51-59%; caries peaks at 0.273 in 1700. Sample 642 individuals across four countries, geographically uneven.

display_label: Decayed teeth start being pulled faster than they are recorded
expected_effect: caries: falls for a non-dietary reason; AMTL: series maximum
measured_effect: Caries 0.273 (1700) -> 0.164 (1800) while AMTL 0.210 -> 0.267, the series maximum. The two move in opposite directions for the first time.

display_label: Amalgam makes tooth repair routine
expected_effect: caries: no longer readable from the tooth
measured_effect: Archaeological intervention prevalence: 1/204 (Pieve di Pava, 10-12th c.), 1/100 (Aberdeen, 1460-1670), 2/450 (Middenbeemster, 1800s). Never above ~1% before 1850.

display_label: Britain equalises sugar duties
expected_effect: caries: acceleration
measured_effect: Duty equalisation precedes the caries peak; no direct dental measurement.

display_label: Roller mills invented; industrial food processing begins
expected_effect: wear: sharp fall; caries: rise
measured_effect: Molar wear 3.28 (1800) -> 2.01 (1915-18), the lowest value in the 1,800-year series. Mechanism: millstones shed grit into flour, steel rollers do not. CAUTION: n=76, one Lithuanian site; wear was already 2.88 at 1700, so the fall is not monotonic.

display_label: Industrial metals reach their modern maximum
expected_effect: metals layer: modern maximum
measured_effect: Modern vs archaeological enamel: Pb 0.63 -> 6.55 (x10.4), Cu 0.25 -> 3.60 (x14.4), Cr 0.072 -> 0.80 (x11.1), Ni 0.24 -> 2.20 (x9.2). Controls barely move and Sr FALLS: Sr 188 -> 168 (x0.89), Ba 3.2 -> 4.6, Zn 145 -> 215. The enamel ran a controlled experiment.

display_label: Fluoride collapses tooth decay - and the tooth cannot show it
expected_effect: NONE MEASURABLE IN THIS PROJECT DATA
measured_effect: Invisible to every layer in this project. GHHP ends 1918; the Kamenov enamel exposure window ends 1975. Known only from national surveys.

display_label: Fillings stop marking the era and start marking the person
expected_effect: intervention layer: the signal decouples from the date
measured_effect: All ages 8.1 -> 6.8. Age 16-24: 7.8 -> 1.7. Age 55-64: 4.9 -> 10.2. The marginal hides the story; the two cohorts cross between 1998 and 2009.

display_label: Intervention becomes near-universal
expected_effect: intervention layer: modern maximum
measured_effect: 84% (n=6470) against archaeological rates of 0.49%, 1.00% and 0.44%. Roughly a 170-fold gap. NOTE: not the same measurement - buried individuals screened for ANY dental work versus living adults examined for fillings.
